lines.text: אית 46 אך
come, to enter. In Chethibh the letter
Yod is transposed so as to read יֵאתוֹן.
אִיתַי Chald. i. q. Heb. יֵשׁ there is,
from which it is derived. Arab. أَيْسٌ,
but only in a few phrases; Syr. ܐܺܝܬ, in
Targg. אִית, Talmud. איתא.—Dan. 5, 11
אִיתַי גְּבַר בְּמַלְכוּתָךְ there is a man in thy
kingdom. 2, 28. 30. 3, 25. With a nega-
tive partic. לָא אִיתַי Dan. 2, 10. 11. 3, 29.
With plur. Dan. 3, 12. In order to ex-
press the various persons of the substan-
tive verb to be, pronouns are suffixed,
mostly in the plural: אִיתוֹהִי he is Dan.
2, 11; אִיתָנָא we are 3, 18; אִיתָיךְ thou
art 2, 26; אִיתֵיכוֹן ye are 3, 14. These
forms construed with a participle, consti-
tute a periphrasis for the finite verb, e. g.
Dan. 3, 18 לָא אִיתָנָא פָּלְחִין we worship
not. Where it stands absolutely, it is
sometimes to be rendered there is, there
exists, il y a, Dan. 2, 10. 11. With dat.
אִיתַי לְ there is to any one, he has, Ezra
אִיתַי pr. n. see אִתַּי.
אִיתִיאֵל (for אִתִּי אֵל, God with me)
pr. n. m. Ithiel, Prov. 30, 1. Ithiel and
Ucal seem to have been children or dis-
ciples of Agur, to whom he addressed
his maxims.
אִיתָמָר (palm-coast) Ithamar, pr. n.
of the youngest son of Aaron, Ex. 6, 23.
אֵיתָן, also אֵתָן Job 33, 19, for יְתָן
with Aleph prosthet. from r. יָתַן to be
perennial, constant.
1. perennity, perpetuity, spoken espec.
of water. Ex. 14, 27 the sea returned
לְאֵיתָנוֹ to its perpetuity i. e. to its perpet-
ual, ceaseless flow. Num. 24, 21 אֵיתָן
מוֹשָׁבֶךָ perpetuity (perpetual) is thy habi-
tation. Joined in the genit. with other
nouns; as נַהֲרוֹת אֵיתָן perennial streams
Ps. 74, 15; נְוֵה אֵיתָן perennial pasture
i. e. ever verdant, Jer. 49, 19. 50, 44;
נַחַל אֵיתָן a perennial brook, ever flowing,
never failing, Deut. 21, 4. Am. 5, 24; and
so without נַחַל, 1 K. 8, 2 יֶרַח הָאֵיתָנִים
the month of flowing brooks, elsewhere
called Tisri, the seventh month of the
Heb. year, from the new moon of October
to the new moon of November. Prov.
13, 15 the way of transgressors אֵיתָן is a
perennial stream, full of water, by which
one may easily be borne away and over-
whelmed.—Job 33, 19 וְרִיב עֲצָמָיו אֵתָן
and the strife in his bones is perpetuity,
perpetual.
2. firmness, strength. Gen. 49, 24 תֵּשֶׁב
בְּאֵיתָן קַשְׁתּוֹ his bow abides in strength,
i. e. is strong, firm. Jer. 5, 15 גּוֹי אֵיתָן
a people of strength, i. e. strong, mighty.
Plur. אֵיתָנִים the strong, the mighty, Vulg.
optimates, Job 12, 19.
3. Ethan, pr. n. an Ezrahite, (see
אֶזְרָחִי,) a wise man 1 K. 5, 11; to whom
Ps. 89 is attributed in the inscription.
אַךְ 1. Part. of affirmation, yea, sure-
ly, certainly, without doubt. Kindr. are
כִּי, כֵּן, אָכֵן, see Hupfeld in Zeitschr. f. d.
Morgenl. II. 143.—Gen. 44, 28 אַךְ טָרֹף
טֹרָף surely-he is torn in pieces. Judg. 3,
18, 21.—Hence
2. Adv. of restriction, limitation, only,
merely. Ex. 10, 17 אַךְ הַפַּעַם only this once.
Lev. 11,21 אַךְ אֶת־זֶה תֹּאכְלוּ only these may
ye eat. Ps. 37, 8 be thou not angry (which
is) only for doing evil, i. e. anger is the
frequent source of evil. Prov. 14, 23
empty talk אַךְ לְמַחְסוֹר (tendeth) only to
penury. 11, 24. 21, 5.—Spec. a) Before
adjectives, where only is equiv. to wholly,
altogether. Deut. 16, 15 וְהָיִיתָ אַךְ שָׂמֵחַ
and thou shalt be only joyful, i. e. shalt
wholly rejoice. Is. 16, 7 אַךְ נְכָאִים wholly
contrite. 19, 11. b) Before substantives,
only, nothing but, where we may render
it alone, merely. Ps. 139, 11 אַךְ חֹשֶׁךְ the
darkness alone, i. e. nothing but the dark-
ness. Ps. 39, 12 אַךְ הֶבֶל nothing but
vanity, merely vanity. c) Before ad-
verbs and verbs, only, i. q. wholly, comp.
above in lett. a. Ps. 73, 13 אַךְ רִיק only in
vain, i. e. wholly in vain. 1 Sam. 25, 21.
Job 19, 13 יֹדְעַי אַךְ זָרוּ מִמֶּנִּי mine ac-
quaintance are wholly estranged from me.
Judg. 20, 39. Job 23, 6. Comp. Ex. 12, 15
אַךְ בַּיּוֹם הָרִאשׁוֹן wholly the first day, i. e.
the very first day, on no other but the
first day.
3. As a particle of exception, only, but,
Gen. 20, 12 אַךְ לֹא בַת אִמִּי only not
(μονονουχί) the daughter of my mother,
i. e. but not. Lev. 11, 4. Num. 26, 55.
Deut. 18, 20. Josh. 3, 4.
4. Of time, only now, i. e. just now,

line_status.note: The running header is pointed: a ḥireq dot is visible under the aleph of אִית (left) and a pataḥ under the aleph plus a shewa inside the final kaf of אַךְ (right). Reading A omits all points; Reading B matches the print.
The printed Hebrew is pointed: a tsere (two dots) is visible beneath the yod and a holem dot above the vav, so יֵאתוֹן (Reading B); Reading A drops the vowel points.
The mark over the final sin is the stacked double-damma (tanwin, ٌ), not a bare fatha: the sequence of superscript marks reads fatha (alif), sukun (ya), dammatan (sin), as in Reading B.

Under the tav of אִיתָנָא the printed point has a vertical stem below the horizontal stroke (T-shape), i.e. qamets, matching the qamets under the following nun; it is not a flat patach as in Reading B. All other characters agree in both readings and match the print.

Decisive point: the vowel under the tav of איתנא. The printed mark has a short vertical stem below the horizontal bar, i.e. qamets (ָ), matching Reading A; Reading B's patach (ַ) would be a plain bar with no stem.

Decisive difference is the printed left-to-right order of the three Hebrew items: the leftmost is כִּי, then כֵּן, then אָכֵן (immediately before ", see"). Reading A reverses the list. Vowel points (dagesh in both כ initials, hiriq/tsere, qamets on א, no dagesh in the כ of אָכֵן) match Reading B as printed.
